stories.title: Will there be a White Christmas this year?
summary: It is just a month until the big day but what do the early signs say about the chances of a white Christmas in the UK?

stories.title: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimer’s in aging mice
summary: A revolutionary new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory performance in aging mice while preventing severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease.
Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory.
Remarkably, the treatment preserved brain function without removing Alzheimer’s-associated plaques, suggesting a completely different way to combat cognitive decline.

stories.title: A black hole the size of an atom could destroy an entire star
summary: MIT scientists have discovered that tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang could slowly devour stars from within, eventually triggering spectacular explosions visible across galaxies.
Detecting these unusual cosmic events could reveal the existence of primordial black holes and help solve the mystery of dark matter.

stories.title: Badger cull ruled out by Welsh government after speculation
summary: Plaid Cymru ministers rule out mass badger cull as part of new plans to tackle bovine tuberculosis.

stories.title: Record 5,200 heat-linked deaths estimated in England this year
summary: The UK Health Security Agency says this year's number of deaths is twice that of the previous record year.

stories.title: Storms targeting both US coasts threaten to snarl Thanksgiving travel for millions
summary: Two storms, including a major Nor'easter on the east coast, are expected to impact millions of people celebrating the holiday with family and friends.

stories.title: 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck reveals an ingenious waterproofing trick
summary: A 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck has revealed sophisticated waterproofing techniques involving pine tar and beeswax.
Microscopic pollen grains trapped in the ancient coatings are now helping scientists reconstruct where the vessel may have traveled and undergone repairs more than two millennia ago.

stories.title: Delia Smith joins opponents of £1.2bn data centre
summary: The TV cook and author is worried about the environmental impact of the proposed Keswick facility.

stories.title: Ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side rewrite the Solar System’s violent past
summary: Scientists studying ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side have uncovered surprising evidence that challenges decades of thinking about the Solar System’s violent past.
Instead of a single catastrophic bombardment, asteroid impacts appear to have declined gradually over billions of years, revealing new clues about Earth's early evolution and the origins of life.

stories.title: Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming.

By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago, signaling the possible start of a new glacial period.
But by the 1960s, rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.

stories.title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake
summary: Tourism and outdated septic tanks are said to be adding to the ecological decline of Buttermere.

stories.title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope
summary: Bagot goats are used to keep vegetation in check and help preserve the view from the Royal Observatory.

stories.title: Earth’s ancient oceans may have fooled scientists about its oxygen history
summary: Earth’s journey from an oxygen-starved world to a planet capable of supporting complex life may have unfolded very differently than scientists once believed.
A new analysis suggests that oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere in three major stages, with the oceans taking millions or even hundreds of millions of years to catch up.

stories.title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
summary: Interests of oil-producing countries, a US boycott and a dispute over finance may have torpedoed climate talks.

stories.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
summary: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.
